newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Primagaz plans to up 97 sales to HUF 22bln.
newsitem.headline: Primagaz plans to up 97 sales to HUF 22bln.

text.p: Hungary's largest liquefied petroleum gas distributor, Primagaz Rt, plans sales of 22 billion forints for this year compared with 17.63 billion forints in 1996, Primagaz CEO Zoltan Szemmelveisz said on Thursday.
"We will continue our expansive investment policy this year," Szemmelveisz told a news conference.
He said that the company's 1996 results, released Thursday, showed a significant improvement over 1995 due both to a cold January-February period in 1996 and to the first return on 1995 investments.
Primagaz will invest some 3.5 billion forints this year, mainly towards further expanding its client base, but is also looking to diversify its activities, Szemmelveisz said.
"We will set up a fifty-fifty joint venture with France's Dehon, aimed at carving out a 30 to 35 percent share of the cooling agent market," he said.
The new company, Frigogaz Kft, with a capital of 45 million forints, will sell environment-friendly cooling agents that will fulfil European Union regulations to be introduced in 2002, he said.
"Our aim is to reach one to 1.5 billion forints turnover within five years," Szemmelveisz said.

Primagaz will also increase by 30 percent the capacity of its 40-60 joint venture with MOL, a facility that transfers Russian gas shipments arriving at Hungary's border with the Ukraine in wide-gauge rail tankers to standard-gauge tankers.

"Although this is a relatively small operation, its strategic importance far outweighs its actual size," Szemmelveisz said. "In the winter months, domestic demand was higher than the transfer capacity."
Primagaz will also start in 1997 a two-year, 350 to 400 million forint project to build an integrated computer system, he added.
Primagaz plans to sell some 270,000 tonnes of gas this year, compared with 250,000 tonnes in 1996, he said.

Last year 195,000 tonnes of gas were sold in cylinders while bulk gas sales accounted for 57,000 to 58,000 tonnes, Szemmelveisz said, but added that the growth of bulk sales would probably decrease this year after doubling both in 1995 and 1996.

Primagaz will stick to its dividend policy established over the last few years, he said, adding that the board would probably recommend the AGM a 15 percent (or 150 forints per share) dividend payment over the 1996 results.
Primagaz is 64.7 percent owned by Netherland's Pam Gas BV, which is owned by SVH Energy NV, a subsidiary of SHV Holdings NV.
Osterreichische Kontrollbank AG holds 5.5 percent in Primagaz and Creditanstalt 4.2 percent.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange, Primagaz shares closed at 10,490 forints, up 440.
